extracted.intended_audience: Twitter/X users, comedians, social-media writers, and creators who want to write funny tweets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing short-form comedy specifically for Twitter/X: structural principles, common joke forms, and a short evaluation rubric to judge whether a tweet will land and spread. Aimed at creators optimizing humor for the platform's constraints and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression Above All
rubrics_metrics.description: The shorter the distance between setup and punchline, the funnier. "Digital lightning bolt — short, sharp, unexpected."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor minimal setups and immediate payoffs; reduce intermediary wording. Aim for crispness and economy — every extra word increases the chance of losing the laugh. Punchlines benefit from immediate juxtaposition after setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline at the End
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the payoff as the final element of the tweet so the reader's attention is carried into the surprise. Avoid burying or front-loading the joke; the explicit rubric asks: "Is the punch at the very end?"

rubrics_metrics.name: 280 Characters Constraint / Brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the tweet under ~280 characters? Brevity forces precision. Every word counts; often single-sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the character limit as a creative constraint: prune modifiers, choose stronger nouns/verbs, and prefer single-sentence constructions where possible. If it's longer than necessary, tighten it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity (Not Generic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it specific (not generic)? Specific detail makes jokes more vivid and shareable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, specific images or situations help readers connect and recognize themselves. Avoid vague generalities; specificity often provides the unexpected twist that generates humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotability / RTability
rubrics_metrics.description: Could it be quote-tweeted with "this"? Quotability drives spread — tweets that can be reused as reactions perform well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft lines that double as punchy reactions or aphorisms. If a short phrase stands alone and resonates, it's more likely to be retweeted or quoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizable Voice / Identifiable POV
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the voice recognizable? Identifiable POV helps tweets feel personal and shareable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a consistent persona or point-of-view so followers know what to expect. Distinctive voice differentiates human tweeting from algorithmic patterns; the rubric explicitly asks if the voice is recognizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise Endings
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprise endings contribute to why Twitter humor spreads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the tweet to set up an expectation and then subvert it with an unexpected final element. Surprise is central to the payoff; predictable or telegraphed endings are weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / Kairos
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage trending topics, memes, and current events to increase relevance and shareability. Timely references should be precise enough that the joke lands for readers encountering it now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Register / Audience Fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Twitter community has its register; stay current on trending topics and memes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone, references, and in-jokes to the specific community you’re addressing. What works on one subcommunity may fall flat or offend in another; tailor language, references, and pacing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Surprise / Avoid Botlike Predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy Bot vs. Human: Bots predictable; humans surprise. Algorithmic patterns get stale; voice matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mechanical joke templates that read like an algorithm. Inject small, odd, or incongruent details that signal human originality. Consistent unpredictability and personality separate effective human-made comedy from bot output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational One-Liner Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational "Did you ever notice…?" type, compressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tight observations about everyday life, compressed into a single line that points out an amusing truth. Keep the setup minimal and the observation precise to maximize relatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misheard / Reframed Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a familiar phrase and twist a word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subvert an expectation by altering a known phrase or idiom. The humor comes from the recognition of the original and the surprise of the alteration; ensure the twist is clear and not overwrought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Deprecating Confession Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal, self-deprecating confession (e.g., "I just spent 45 minutes pretending to be busy so my dog wouldn't think I'm boring").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modesty and vulnerability to invite empathy and laughter. Keep it specific and crisp; avoid long backstories that dilute the bite of the confession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain Mash-Up Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply rules from one domain to another absurdly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend two disparate domains (e.g., corporate speak + parenting) to reveal absurdities. The juxtaposition should be clear and the mapping between domains tight enough to make the incongruity humorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply / Quote-Tweet Format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the context of someone else's tweet to add a concise, pointed counterpoint or twist. Effective replies often rely on the original text as setup; ensure your line is readable and funny both in-context and when viewed alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Pun / Image + Text Combo
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual Pun: Image + text combo (when text alone won't carry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair imagery with a short caption when the visual element completes or sharpens the joke. Ensure the image is clear at thumbnail size and that the combination still reads quickly for scrolling audiences.
